key_insight: Medical encoder pretraining works better when web text is filtered for dense medical terminology and optionally rewritten to make medical signals more explicit.
clinical_relevance: This could improve French medical NLP systems such as clinical entity recognition and other downstream tasks by making pretraining data more medically informative.
method: Filtered web documents by medical-term density to enrich medical content.
Used an LLM to rephrase documents into denser, signal-amplified versions with broader entity context.
Combined filtering and rephrasing to build the FineMed pretraining corpus and train DoctoBERT.
evidence_signal: On French medical NLP benchmarks, the medical-term density filter beat a common educational-quality filter, and mixing filtered web data with signal-amplifying rephrasing gave the largest improvement.
watch_item: LLM-based rephrasing and web-data filtering may introduce bias or artifacts, so the added signal should be checked carefully for fidelity and downstream reliability.
paper_title: Where Does the Signal Live? A Web Data Recipe for Medical Encoder Pretraining
